summary: Humberto Maturana was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chile, University College London, and Harvard University. He held posts at MIT, the University of Chile, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and founded the Instituto Matríztica in 2000.
Humphrey William Codrington worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Winchester College and New College before serving in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1903 to 1932.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard. He held faculty posts at Harvard and the University of Chicago, as well as appointments at NYU, Oxford, and the Smart Museum.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

Huston Smith worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Central Methodist University, the University of Chicago, and under Zuigan Goto, later holding posts at Denver, Washington University, MIT, Syracuse University, and UC Berkeley.

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010), studying under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.
Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts as a professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Hyacinth Bitchurin was a scholar in sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at Kazan Theological Academy. He taught there, served as rector at Tobolsk Seminary, worked as an interpreter, and was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, Aoyama Gakuin University, and The Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, Choi served as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara (attested 2015).
Hyla Stuntz Converse was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned degrees from Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. She held a post at Oklahoma State University in 1974.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Yale University, the University of Freiburg, and Harvard University. He also studied under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon from around 1990 to 2004.

Hyoung Seok Ham works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Ham studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Michigan (PhD) under Madhav M. Deshpande, later holding posts at Kyushu University and Chonnam National University.

Hywel David Lewis worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University, and Jesus College, Oxford, and held a academic post at Bangor University from circa 1936 to 1955.

Hélène Brunner-Lachaux was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jean Filliozat. She held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge. He serves as Professor and Principal Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Harris was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Cambridge and Lancaster University. He held academic posts at St Martin's College, St Hugh's College, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Cumbria.

Ian James Coghlan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).

Ian Kesarcodi-Watson was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Melbourne, Oxford, McMaster (under John G. Arapura), and Pune. He held lectureships in philosophy at the University of Hong Kong and La Trobe University.
